title: Who Will Win Game of the Year? Here's the Inside Scoop
summary:
Get your controllers ready! The 13th Game Awards are happening on December 10, and everyone is guessing which game will win the top prize: Game of the Year.

Right now, the smart money is on Resident Evil Requiem. It's a scary action game that critics really like. It has a score of about 89 out of 100 on Metacritic, a website that collects reviews. The Game Awards usually love games like this — big, cinematic adventures with a strong story.

But watch out for Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave. It's a strategy role-playing game from Nintendo. Fans and critics are excited because it mixes great storytelling with fun combat. No strategy game has ever been nominated for Game of the Year before. Could this be the first?

Then there's 007 First Light, a James Bond game. It lets you sneak around and be a spy. It scored 87 on Metacritic. Licensed games — games based on movies or books — almost never get nominated. But this one might break the rule.

One thing is for sure: it's a weird year for games. Some big titles flopped, so the race is wide open. Who will take home the trophy? We'll find out in December!
why_it_matters: If you play games, this is like the Super Bowl of games — it tells you which games are worth trying, and it shows that a game from a type of genre that usually gets ignored can still win the biggest prize.

background_read: The Game Awards is a big yearly show where prizes are handed out for the best games, and the top prize is called Game of the Year.
Resident Evil is a famous scary game series (made by the Japanese company Capcom) that has been around since the 1990s, so a new Resident Evil game already has lots of fans.
James Bond, or 007, is a famous British spy from books and movies, which is why a James Bond game is a 'licensed' game.
Nintendo is the Japanese company that makes Mario, Zelda and the Switch console, and it also makes the Fire Emblem games.
Article_Structure: WHO: Games fans, critics and three main contenders: Resident Evil Requiem, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave and 007 First Light.
WHAT: The 13th Game Awards will name the Game of the Year on December 10, and people are guessing who will win.
WHERE: On the awards show itself, with review scores coming from Metacritic, a website that collects critics' reviews.
WHY: No one is sure who will win, because some big games flopped and unusual games — a strategy game and a licensed game — might be nominated for the first time.

perspectives.description: They feel confident, because their game got great reviews and looks like the kind of big, movie-like adventure the awards usually love.
They are excited because no strategy game has ever been nominated for Game of the Year, so this could be a big first.
They point out that award shows often favour big, flashy games, so smaller or unusual games can get left out even when they are really good.
